paras: In a lake lived a tortoise named Kambugriva. His two dearest friends were a pair of swans, Sankata and Vikata. Every evening the swans sat on the shore and listened to the tortoise, who loved to talk more than anything in the world.

One year the rains failed. Day by day the lake shrank, until only a muddy puddle remained. “We must fly to a great lake far away,” said the swans sadly. “But how will you come with us, dear friend? You cannot fly.”
The tortoise thought hard. “Bring a strong stick,” he said. “I will hold the middle tightly in my mouth. You two hold the ends in your beaks and carry me through the sky.”
“It is a clever plan,” said the swans, “but remember: you must not open your mouth, not even once, until we land. If you speak, you will fall.”
“I promise,” said the tortoise. “I will not say a single word.”

So the swans rose into the air with the stick, and the tortoise swung between them, high above fields and villages. Down below, the people of a town looked up in amazement. “Look! Look!” they shouted. “Two birds are carrying a tortoise on a stick!” Children ran through the streets, laughing and pointing.

The tortoise grew annoyed. “Why are these people making such a fuss?” he thought. “I must tell them to mind their own business!” He forgot his promise and opened his mouth: “What are you all staring at—”
Before he could finish, he lost his grip on the stick and tumbled down, down, down to the ground.
Moral: Know when to keep silent. Those who cannot hold their tongue often bring trouble on themselves.
